title: Tracing for long-lived generator sessions: SDK weave + handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Enable reliable trace continuity and low-overhead instrumentation for long-lived generator/streaming sessions (e.g., chat streaming, token generators, and background continuation jobs). Deliver a cross-language SDK pattern that weaves an active span into an ongoing generator, supports safe handoff to background workers or async continuations, and minimizes runtime allocations and hot-path latency.
background: Current SDK tracing hooks assume short-lived request/response lifecycles. Generator/streaming flows break those assumptions: spans live across many yield points, may be checkpointed and resumed in different processes/threads, and can be resumed by web workers or serverless continuations. This ticket explores a pragmatic, production-safe approach that preserves span fidelity while avoiding amplification of sampling and tail-latency artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: SDK pattern defined for JS, Python, and Go that allows embedding a light-weight generator span token into generator objects without copying cold KV state
End-to-end trace continuity demonstrated across a generator being resumed in a background worker process (HTTP -> queue -> worker) with <5ms additional p50 latency in the hot path
Sampling semantics preserved: generator-resumed spans do not double-count or bypass sampling budget; observed sampling rate matches parent requests within 1% in synthetic tests
Unit and integration tests covering edge cases: abrupt cancellation, dual-resume, multiple yield hops, and worker crash/retry
Design doc and SDK examples published to Confluence and developer SDK repo; at least one public example in examples/chat-streaming demonstrating full trace in Console trace viewer
work_items: Design proposal for 'weave token' format and lifetime semantics
Prototype JS SDK helper: attachWeaveToken(generator, spanContext)
Prototype Python SDK helper: generator_context_wrapper(generator, spanContext)
Prototype Go SDK helper: StreamSpanCarrier and ShallowToken serializer
Queue worker integration test (Redis queue) to validate handoff and resume
Benchmarking harness for hot-path latency and memory allocations
Add trace viewer annotations to Console: mark generator start/resume/finish
Prepare e2e sample app and docs; add a code snippet to SDK README
decisions: Use a compact 'weave token' that encodes span id, trace id, sampled bit, and a monotonic resume-sequence; token is base64 URL-safe string
Token is intentionally shallow: no full span serialization, avoids carrying baggage beyond id; heavy metadata is fetched on resume via a small lookup from the control-plane shard if needed
Worker-side resume will create a child span (resume-span) linked to original trace-id to preserve causal graph without resurrecting parent span object
Sampling decision follows original parent sampled bit; if parent not sampled, resume spans remain non-sampled to prevent sampling budget leakage
Default SDK helpers opt-in (not automatic) to avoid breaking existing tracing semantics for customers with custom instrumentation
progress_updates: 2026-02-17: Initial design sync with SDK leads (JS/Python/Go). Agreed on shallow token approach to minimize runtime cost.
2026-02-22: JS prototype implemented (attachWeaveToken) and smoke-tested against local stream server. Verified token size ~48 bytes.
2026-03-01: Python wrapper implemented; found race when generator canceled during async handoff — added cancellation sentinel handling.
2026-03-05: Benchmarks show JS hot-path p50 increased by 3.2ms with naive token attach; optimized to 0.9ms by moving serialization off critical path.
2026-03-08: Integration test for queue handoff passing in staging; traces show resume-span as child of original; missing Console annotation work remains.
2026-03-10: Security review flagged potential leak where tokens could be logged by naive apps; added docs and SDK helper to scrub tokens from default logger format.
review_comments: Linda Chen (Platform PM): 'Can we ensure the default sampling preservation is clearly documented for customers using manual sampling? We should add a migration note.'
Sanjay Rao (Reliability): 'Verify behavior under high fanout where a single generator spawns many resumes — need to ensure resume operation can't amplify traffic to control plane.'
Elena Martinez (Security): 'Token format must be revocable and short-lived if it can be persisted; recommend adding an optional expiry field and control-plane revocation list.'
Marco Diaz (Assignee): 'Implementing expiry as a resume-sequence TTL and optional revocation lookup; will add tests for expired token resume denial.'
risks: Leaked tokens in logs or persisted generator checkpoints could expose trace IDs; mitigated by default logger scrubbing and optional token TTL.
High fanout of resumed generators could create many child spans and increase telemetry costs; mitigation: heuristics in SDK and server to collapse resume spikes in Console and samples.
Cross-language token compatibility edge cases (endianness, base64 libs); mitigation: uniform canonical encoding tests in CI for all three SDKs.
testing_plan: Integration test: HTTP request -> generator start -> enqueue token -> worker resume -> assert trace continuity in telemetry backend
Fault injection: worker crash on resume and retry path verifying idempotent behavior
Load test: simulate 10k concurrent generator sessions with randomized yields to assess telemetry amplification
E2E sanity: example chat-streaming app traces visible in Console with generator lifecycle annotations
rollout_plan: Feature gated: opt-in flag in SDK minor version (rc) -> experimental users only
Run with 'observability-experiments' cohort in staging for 2 weeks
Collect metrics: resume success rate, added p50 latency, sampled span counts
Gradual enablement: 5% -> 25% -> 100% for SDK minor release channels after safety checks
Add migration doc and 'how to disable' troubleshooting guide
